query: How does retrieval-augmented generation compare to fine-tuned biomedical language models for evidence-based question answering?

top_papers.title: Large language model
top_papers.abstract:
A large language model (LLM) is a neural network trained on a vast amount of text for natural language processing tasks, especially language generation. LLMs can generate, summarize, translate and parse text in many contexts, and are a foundational technology behind modern chatbots. Biased or inaccurate training data can make an LLM's output less reliable.

top_papers.title: Language model benchmark
top_papers.abstract:
A language model benchmark is a standardized test designed to evaluate the performance of language models on various natural language processing tasks. These tests are intended for comparing different models' capabilities in areas such as language understanding, generation, and reasoning.
